A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeQA-Score study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-quality regression and distribution-prediction results, ablations, and the Q-Bench extension experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Equation (4) adds a leading minus sign to sum_i p_i log(p_i^pred/p_i), correcting the specified level-token training loss. This is a limited correction to the written objective; the architecture, soft-label construction, fidelity loss, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or retraining.

E1.justification: The training and evaluation coverage is identical, including the main IQA datasets, additional AIGC datasets in Table A4, and Q-Instruct/Q-Bench tasks in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. This includes the single-dataset baselines in Table 3, Q-Align comparisons, and LIQE and Compare2Score in Table A5.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same dataset partition descriptions, score normalization, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and testing procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The soft-label, fidelity-loss, level-text, level-number, and component-training ablations are unchanged. The qualitative cases and score-regression/quality-description transfer analyses in Appendices C–D are also retained.

E5.justification: Annotation-variance reporting, predicted score distributions, and the parameter-dispersion statistics in Table 2 are unchanged. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and A1–A9 and the qualitative predictions in the figures are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains DeQA-Score's KonIQ PLCC/SRCC of 0.953/0.941, and Table A8 retains score-pretraining overall accuracy of 0.7258.

T1.justification: The minus sign added in Equation (4) changes the expression from negative KL divergence to the intended KL divergence loss. This corrects a mathematical definition; the other equations, Gaussian assumptions, and appendix derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning distribution-based soft labels, fidelity-loss co-training, score-regression performance, and alignment with human score distributions.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning quality-description co-training, errors for small score variances, and high memory consumption.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain the same, including PIPAL pseudo-variance construction, the small-variance fallback, optimizer settings, hardware, training times, and the code/model release link.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to Q-Align, UNIQUE, and prior MLLM-based IQA methods.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliation text and replaces several appendix references with section references. Appendix C also changes the clear reference 'Figs. 6 and A3 to A5' to the ambiguous 'Figs. A3 to 6.' The narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 now visibly includes the L_fd symbol beside the fidelity-loss connection and slightly adjusts label typography. The figure and table inventory, arrangement, and overall page layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (4) makes the written training objective consistent with the stated KL-divergence loss, reducing the risk of implementing it with the wrong sign. Figure 5 also gains a useful loss label. These limited gains outweigh the worsened figure cross-reference in Appendix C; the empirical evidence and scientific scope remain unchanged.
